title: Routing/Auth/Quota odd-hours standup notes + sprint kickoff
content:
Date: 2027-11-03
Type: Odd-hours cross-squad standup (routing / auth / quotas) + quick sprint kickoff fragment
Facilitator: Maya Chen
Attendees: Maya, Omar R., Priya, Lena, Devon (+ joined later: Jules from SRE)
Location: #pltfm-routing-auth Slack huddle -> notes captured here

Agenda:
- Rapid health check (control plane / router / auth)
- Follow-up on overnight quota bleed-through spikes
- Auth cert rotation fallout hypothesis and rollback status
- Small scope sprint kickoff: short tasks for next 48h to stabilize canaries

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Canary incidents last 6 hours show a routing allocator imbalance causing 2.3x latency tail on small customers; believed related to a heuristic change pushed in PR 2162.
- Quota bookkeeping showed temporary double-counting for burst windows (bleed-through) -> visible as excess quota consumption in several customers (PLT-3087).
- Auth cert rotation deployed to staging and partially to prod; a subset of older clients failed to follow new TLS cipher list -> temporary 401/403 for token refresh flow; rollback initiated and certs reissued for affected pool.
- Immediate plan: pin allocator kernel to previous build on dedicated pools, hotfix quota counter to dedupe burst events, and complete auth cert rollback + compat shim.

Notes by area:
1) Control plane / routing allocator (Omar)
- Observed: allocator drift started ~02:10 UTC, manifested as skewed assignment for small-seq requests. Canary traffic (10% sample) saw request scheduling concentrated on 2 nodes leading to batching blowup and higher p90/p99.
- Suspect cause: recent change that prefers node-local caches more aggressively (PR 2162) interacts poorly with our small-request distribution.
- Data: p50 stable, p90 +40%, p99 +130% for canary group between 02:15-03:40 UTC.
- Mitigation taken: rolled allocator selector to previous commit on canary group at 03:50 UTC; metrics normalized in ~20 minutes.
- Next: create a focused test to replay small-sequence distribution (workload generator) and add invariant test for cache-locality skew. Owner: Omar. Ticket: PLT-3091 (new).

2) Quotas and billing counters (Lena)
- Symptom: several accounts reported unexpected quota exhaustion despite low true request volume. Debug log shows duplicate quota increments for burst window when route fallback triggers synchronous requeue path.
- Temporary fix: added dedupe window at quota adapter (feature flagged) and turned it on for affected orgs. Flag key: quota.dedupe.burst.v1.
- Root cause hypothesis: fallback path increments before primary path completes; race condition.
- Plan: implement a canonical request id for a single evaluation pass and update metrics; longer-term: refactor fallback to be non-incremental. Owner: Lena. Related ticket: PLT-3087.

3) Auth (Priya)
- Incident: cert rotation pushed new cipher suites and disabled some older client compat bits. Token refresh endpoints returned 401 for a subset of SDK versions.
- Rollback: rolled to previous cert bundle for prod pool A at 03:30 UTC. For the rest of the pools we staged a compat shim to accept older ciphers for 72h while we notify customers.
- Action: run a token refresh compatibility sweep across commonly used SDK builds and add gating test to deploy pipeline. Owner: Priya. Ticket: PLT-3092.

4) Canary & observability (Devon + SRE)
- Observability gaps identified: missing correlation id on allocator scheduling logs made root cause blurring harder. Added a correlation id to the allocator pipeline (hot patch) and phased into canary.
- Dashboard: created temporary chart 'allocator.skew.by-request-size' and 'quota.duplicate.increment.rate' on Console Quick View.
- Alert tuning: silenced noisy alert on quota.backfill for 1 hour while we roll the dedupe flag.

Metrics snapshot (quick plaintext table):
- Canary sample rate: 10%
- Allocator p50/p90/p99 (baseline -> impacted window -> post-rollout):
  - baseline: 22ms / 48ms / 210ms
  - impacted: 24ms / 72ms / 480ms
  - post-rollout: 21ms / 50ms / 230ms
- Quota duplicate increment rate: baseline ~0.01% -> spike 0.9% during incident -> reduced to 0.03% after dedupe flag
- Auth token refresh error rate (affected SDKs): peaked at 6.8% -> rolled back to 0.1%

Decisions made in meeting:
- Rollback allocator selector on full production until we have unit + replay tests for small-request distribution. (Owner: Omar)
- Keep quota dedupe flag enabled for affected orgs while we rework fallback path. (Owner: Lena)
- Reissue compat certs and enable 72h shim; customers to be notified via CS playbook. (Owner: Priya)
- Add correlation id to new log invariant and require presence for any future scheduling-related change. (Owner: Devon)

Sprint kickoff (micro-sprint for next 48h):
- PLT-3091 (Omar): Add workload generator + unit tests for allocator; WIP MR due EOD 11/04.
- PLT-3093 (Lena): Quota canonical id + dedupe hardening; feature-flag remove plan doc by 11/05.
- PLT-3092 (Priya): Auth compat sweep test matrix + deploy gate; PR to add gate by 11/04.
- PLT-3094 (Devon): Observability: add allocator correlation id across trace/span and wire to Console. PR + dashboard tile by 11/05.
- Quick spike: Jake (SRE) to run chaos replay of fallback path to validate quota fix in staging.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Why did PR 2162 not surface in our scheduler canary? Need to review canary sampling rules and whether small-seq workload is underrepresented. (Action: Omar + Devops)
- Should we automatically throttle selector change rollouts by request-size distribution? Explore algorithmic guardrails. (Action: team brainstorm next sync)
- Customer comms: CS needs a one-pager summary and recommended mitigations for affected accounts. (Owner: Maya -> coordinate with CS)

Action items (short):
- Omar: PLT-3091 allocator test + fix (due 11/04)
- Lena: PLT-3093 quota canonical id + plan (due 11/05)
- Priya: PLT-3092 auth compat tests + gate (due 11/04)
- Devon: PLT-3094 add correlation id + dashboard (due 11/05)
- Jake (SRE): chaos replay of fallback path in staging (start 11/04)
- Maya: Draft CS one-pager and thread to #customer-success (due 11/04)

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Investigate adding 'request-size' histogram to all canary sampling keys (would have caught this earlier).
- Consider a "prefer stability" rollout policy that biases away from selector changes during high churn windows (end of month deployments).

Meeting end: 04:10 UTC. Next mini-sync: 2027-11-04 16:00 PT (focus: review PLT-3091 test results).

Attachments referenced in thread: link to Linear tickets and PRs above.

---
History: this doc is the odd-hours capture and sprint fragment for follow-up; will be moved into weekly control plane roundup if no new incidents appear by 11/05.
